clue.text: Go through the motions, as clocks do

definitions.meaning: to act busily while making no progress, like soldiers marching on the spot
a clock records the passing hours, ticking them off

explanation.surface: Someone merely going through the motions, as mechanically as a ticking clock.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to stall without advancing and, literally, to register the hours, which is what clocks are for.

clue.text: Harry, the spy over the way

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the spy sits above the next piece

parts.note: a mole is a spy planted inside an organisation
St, street, is a way

explanation.surface: A spy across the road is bothering someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like a name but is the verb, to harass.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry someone is to pester and harass them.

clue.text: What VIP gets in Northern resort? The sulks

parts.note: Redcar is a seaside resort in North Yorkshire, in the north of England
a pet is a fit of sulking, as in 'in a pet'

explanation.surface: A celebrity sulking at a northern English seaside town.
explanation.definitionFit: Dignitaries are welcomed by unrolling a crimson rug for them to walk on.

clue.text: In which you once took in a form of art

definitions.text: In which you once took in a form of art

indicators.note: the old word for you takes in, contains, the next piece

parts.note: thee is an old form of you

indicators.note: a form of a word is that word reshaped, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A place where people of old went to see an art form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a form of' signals the anagram; the whole clue also describes the place, since in it people once watched an art form.
explanation.definitionFit: Drama is staged in this building, and it is itself an art form.

clue.text: Crop worked on by Daedalus, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is identified by its spoken sound

parts.note: in Greek myth Daedalus built the labyrinth, a maze, for King Minos

explanation.surface: A harvest supposedly tended by the mythical craftsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Corn on the cob is a cereal crop grown in fields.

clue.text: Fruit drink

definitions.meaning: botanically a gourd such as a marrow or pumpkin is a fruit
a British soft drink of fruit concentrate diluted with water

explanation.surface: A bare shopping note: a fruit-flavoured drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A gourd plant's produce goes by this name, and so does the cordial British children dilute with water.

clue.text: Don to some degree accepts neat come-uppance

indicators.note: the word for to some degree accepts, holds inside, the next piece

parts.note: quite means to some degree, fairly

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox

explanation.surface: A university don partly accepts that a tidy punishment is deserved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' looks like an academic, but it is Don Quixote; 'come-uppance' turns OX into XO.
explanation.definitionFit: Cervantes' deluded knight is known by the Spanish title Don.

clue.text: Take a drink about tea-time, and get charged

indicators.note: the drink goes about, around, the next piece

parts.note: ale is a drink of beer
IV is four in Roman numerals, four o'clock being tea-time

explanation.surface: Having a drink around tea-time and getting the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: IV is four in Roman numerals, and four o'clock is the British tea-time; 'charged' means carrying current, not billed.
explanation.definitionFit: A live wire carries electric current.

clue.text: Get intoxicated on a shot of this drink

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: to get high is to become intoxicated
a ball is a shot in games such as cricket or tennis

explanation.surface: Getting drunk on a single shot of some liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall mixed drink of spirits and soda served in a tall glass.

clue.text: Trading in Southern part of London

parts.note: Wapping is a district of East London by the Thames

explanation.surface: Doing business in a district of south London.
explanation.definitionFit: Exchanging goods with one another is a form of commerce.

clue.text: Indian laws — 11 get broken by some appearing in court

indicators.note: laws that get broken are smashed apart, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
printed as 11 but read as II, the Roman numeral for two

explanation.surface: Some laws in India are flouted by people turning up in court.
explanation.walkthrough: '11' looks like a cross-reference to 11 across, but it is the Roman numeral II. 'get broken' asks for INDIANLAWS + II + GET to be rearranged; the court is a royal one, not a law court.
explanation.definitionFit: A royal court is attended by noblewomen who serve the queen, so these attendants appear at court.

clue.text: Take up residence outside a city in America

indicators.note: the word for settling down is placed outside, wrapped round the next piece

parts.note: to take up residence somewhere is to settle there

explanation.surface: Someone moving to live just outside a US city.
explanation.definitionFit: Seattle is a major port city in Washington State, USA.

clue.text: Saw rambler in the lead

indicators.note: the rambler is placed in, within, the symbol for lead

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead, from Latin plumbum
a rover is a wanderer or rambler

explanation.surface: A walker seen out in front of the group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a past tense verb but is the noun: an old saying.
explanation.definitionFit: An old saw is a traditional saying or maxim.

clue.text: Social activities causing a crush at "The King and I"

parts.note: a press is a crowded throng, a crush
K is the abbreviation for king, as in chess

explanation.surface: A crush of people at a performance of the musical The King and I.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase for 'after skiing' names the evening socialising at a ski resort.

clue.text: Mineolas used to make dessert

indicators.note: used to make another word, the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Citrus fruits going into a pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: A mineola is a citrus fruit, a type of tangelo.
explanation.definitionFit: Semolina milk pudding is a traditional British dessert.

clue.text: Without money, about to crack up

parts.note: ex means without or excluding, as in ex dividend

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for money reads backwards

parts.note: a lot is a large sum, plenty of money

explanation.surface: Someone without money about to have a breakdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crack up' suggests collapse, but here it means praise, as in 'not all it's cracked up to be'.
explanation.definitionFit: To crack something up is to praise it highly.

clue.text: Dirt — earth that's loose, of poor quality

indicators.note: loose soil is scattered and shifted, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Crumbly soil is of inferior grade.
explanation.definitionFit: Something third-class is mediocre and inferior.

clue.text: Jack of all trades in reality taking round breadbasket

parts.note: a fact is something real
O is round in shape
breadbasket is slang for the stomach, the tum

explanation.surface: A handyman really carrying a breadbasket around.
explanation.definitionFit: A factotum is a servant or employee who does all kinds of work.

clue.text: Greek story

definitions.meaning: relating to Athens or the region of Attica
American spelling of storey: a room at the top floor of a house

explanation.surface: Just a Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means Athenian, and also the top storey or loft of a house.

clue.text: Seeds produced by this coach constantly

parts.note: a railway coach is a car
away means continually, as in 'chatting away'

explanation.surface: Seeds grown on the carriage all the time.
explanation.definitionFit: These are aromatic seeds used to flavour bread and cakes.

clue.text: Mrs Ravenal's main goal wrecked

indicators.note: a wrecked object is broken up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman's chief ambition has been ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: Magnolia Hawks marries Gaylord Ravenal in the musical Show Boat; the 's is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In Show Boat the heroine becomes Mrs Ravenal on marrying the gambler Gaylord Ravenal.

clue.text: Watch the position of one's bishop

definitions.meaning: to supervise or keep an eye on
a bishop is in charge of, over, his diocese, his see

explanation.surface: Keep an eye on where your chess bishop stands.
explanation.definitionFit: To supervise means to watch over; read as two words it puts the bishop over his diocese.

clue.text: Extremely boring mortal

explanation.surface: Someone tediously dull and only human.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means tediously dull, and also lethal.

clue.text: Open vehicle protected to some extent by giant umbrellas

indicators.note: says the answer is sheltered partly inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An open carriage shaded by big umbrellas.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'protected' into the definition; the definition is 'Open vehicle', and 'protected to some extent by' signals the hidden run.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumbrel is an open two-wheeled cart, famously used to carry victims to the guillotine.

clue.text: Mark exam, knowing what is right and wrong

definitions.text: knowing what is right and wrong

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for the German mark
an oral is a spoken exam

explanation.surface: Marking an exam paper, aware of what is correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a verb but is the old German currency.
explanation.definitionFit: A principled person has an ethical sense of good and bad.

clue.text: Try to persuade the west to listen to the French

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for west
to heed advice is to listen to it
le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: An appeal for western nations to pay attention to France.
explanation.definitionFit: To coax is to use flattery to get someone to do something.

clue.text: You've no right to twist a girl

indicators.note: no right means the letter for right is taken away

parts.note: to wrench is to twist

explanation.surface: A warning that you have no business twisting a girl's arm.
explanation.definitionFit: Wench is an old or jocular word for a young woman.

clue.text: Strike when iron's hot, and surrender

indicators.note: to strike something is to hit and reshape it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored
taken as written

explanation.surface: The blacksmith's proverb to strike while the iron is hot, then give up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike when iron's hot' reads as the blacksmith's proverb, but 'Strike' is the anagram signal, and the 'and' that seems to join two ideas supplies the final letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To give up a card game by discarding your cards is to concede, so the idiom means to give up.

clue.text: Scholar accepted a bet in the States

indicators.note: the scholar accepts, takes inside, the next pieces

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, is a scholar
to lay is to bet, as in laying odds

explanation.surface: An academic agreeing to a wager in the USA.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the States' suggests America, but it means the Federated Malay States.
explanation.definitionFit: The former British colony was made up of the Federated and Unfederated Malay States.

clue.text: This cut down each sort of crime

indicators.note: cut down means shortened, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: every means each

explanation.surface: This reduces every kind of crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealing is a particular category of offence.
